correctness.rationale: Every square-zero dual matrix is A+epsilon B with A^2=0 and AB+BA=0. A square-zero rank-r residue has normal form J2^r plus zeros. Direct block multiplication gives all B with dimension n^2-2r(n-r); Smith elimination leaves epsilon times an independent s-by-s block T. Image/kernel flag counting and the standard exact rank formula yield C(n,q;r,t). Summably small weight deviations give uniform residue-rank limit; conditional corank bounds give the independent discrete limit. The package script exhaustively checks all matrices for seven small prime-field configurations, including q=2,n=3; these computations do not replace proof.

value.rationale: The exact Smith module-type statistics answer a natural matrix-polynomial question at the repeated-root boundary excluded by square-free ring enumerations. More significantly, the lifting fiber dimension cancels the classical rank-dependent field exponent, creating a uniform macroscopic residue-rank law and an independent universal corank limit. This qualitative change is an intrinsically motivated infinite-family structural statement, not an arbitrary finite cutoff.
